notes: Independent review performed 7 November 2026 using fresh curl downloads, local PyMuPDF text extraction, visual inspection of scanned tables/drawings/transcript pages, and GeographicLib recomputation. The 173 grouped checks comprise 29 core descriptive fields/claims, all 11 numbers entries, 15 priority events (zero-based events[6], [7], [13], [14], [15], [18], [19], [20], [21], [22], [23], [24], [26], [27], [34]), the sole non-null verbatim quote, 28 perspective claim/evidence/ending paragraphs, all 78 radar rows including their geographic conversions, eight direction-block point/timing/build-note checks, the menu line, and two source-date checks. Composite entries count once; URL availability checks are excluded from this count. All 27 source-list URLs returned HTTP 200, with actual PDF signatures for PDF sources; the FAA aircraft photograph also returned HTTP 200 and was viewed. s27 resolves through a valid redirect. People totals, aircraft identification/engines/reference dimensions, approximate site and wreckage bounds, route endpoints, one_line and status_why agree with the inspected sources. Boeing's conflicting metric length label is already disclosed; the explicit imperial conversion is arithmetically correct. Airport reference coordinates/elevations match the cited OurAirports CSV, which is a secondary current reference rather than primary proof of historical 1996 airport geometry. The cockpit quote is a continuous verbatim excerpt, correctly attributed to the left-seat captain: s6 transcript printed p. 52 (PDF p. 53), also s1 printed p. 2. The omitted subsequent words are outside the quoted excerpt. EDT-to-UTC conversions correctly add four hours and roll over to 18 July; the FDR/CVR correlation and power-loss window are accurately distinguished. All 78 computed radar coordinate pairs reproduce the supplied X/Y values to their stated rounding; three input transcriptions are erroneous as listed. The other 75 selected radar rows agree with the scanned source table. The final whole-second FDR row and its five values in numbers[4] agree with s2 printed p. 42. This was not a sample-by-sample audit of all 72 FDR rows. All four perspectives preserve the distinction between official findings, rejected advocacy and modelling limits. The 38 inconsistent witness accounts, three residue-positive pieces, unknown residue origin, radar limitations and uncertainty about ignition are supported. The 2013 petition and 2014 rejection were inspected directly; the 2026 FBI extract reports early unverified leads, not an authenticated attack. No new cause can be inferred from that extract or the archive finding aid. The full 415-page FOIA production and approximately 1,900-page archive collection were not inspected. The TWA800 direction block has no overlays or endTitle fields. Its four source references all resolve to s1 in this dataset; model timing and the schematic build-note qualification are supported, subject to the bank-angle error reported above. Exact invented schematic pitch/position values are not certified as measurements. The menu label is consistent with the established tank explosion and subsequent disputed theories. No passenger is named in the research data or TWA800 direction/menu text, and no gratuitous victim detail was found. Input research files were not edited.
